name: Delivery Channel Risk
description: Inherent-risk factors in how customers are acquired and served. Covers non-face-to-face relationships, intermediaries and introducers, remote onboarding and reliance on third parties.

sources.text: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach (sector-specific guidance series, general principles)
FATF Recommendations, Recommendation 1 and Interpretive Note (assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach)
Wolfsberg Group, Guidance on a Risk Based Approach for Managing Money Laundering Risks (2006)

exposure.rationale: Generic channel risk: non-face-to-face onboarding, introducers and third-party reliance.

indicators.name: Non-face-to-face relationship
indicators.desc: Customer is onboarded and serviced without any in-person contact.
indicators.ctx: Customer is onboarded and serviced without any in-person contact.
indicators.fp: Digital channels are the norm for many.

indicators.name: Use of introducers or intermediaries
indicators.desc: Customers originate from agents, brokers or introducers who may not apply adequate checks.
indicators.ctx: Customers originate from agents, brokers or introducers who may not apply adequate checks.
indicators.fp: Intermediaries are standard in many industries.

indicators.name: Reliance on third-party CDD
indicators.desc: Institution relies on another entity's due diligence without testing it.
indicators.ctx: Institution relies on another entity's due diligence without testing it.
indicators.fp: Reliance is permitted when conditions are met.

indicators.name: Remote onboarding with weak verification
indicators.desc: Onboarding relies on a single image or unverified selfie, with no database check.
indicators.ctx: Onboarding relies on a single image or unverified selfie, with no database check.

indicators.name: High volume of onboarding from single source
indicators.canon: Spike in volume via a single channel, agent or source
indicators.desc: Unusual surge in accounts or claims originating from one channel, introducer, agent, IP range or device.
indicators.ctx: Unusual surge of accounts via one channel, introducer, IP range or device.
indicators.fp: Campaigns and partnerships cause legitimate spikes.

indicators.name: Anonymous or masked access
indicators.desc: Use of VPN, proxy, anonymising tools or emulators when accessing services.
indicators.ctx: Use of VPN, proxy, anonymising tools or emulators when accessing services.

indicators.name: Agent or branch network with weak oversight
indicators.canon: Agent or branch network with weak oversight
indicators.desc: Distributed agents operate with inconsistent controls or limited supervision.
indicators.ctx: Distributed agents operate with inconsistent controls or limited supervision.

indicators.name: Account opened by third party on customer's behalf
indicators.canon: Account opened by third party on customer's behalf
indicators.desc: Application completed by someone other than the customer without clear authority.
indicators.ctx: Application completed by someone other than the customer without clear authority.
indicators.fp: Guardians and professional representatives act lawfully.

indicators.name: Channel used inconsistent with customer profile
indicators.canon: Channel used inconsistent with customer profile
indicators.desc: Customer uses channels atypical for them, such as a distant branch or sudden switch to digital.
indicators.ctx: Customer uses channels atypical for them, such as a distant branch or sudden switch to digital.
indicators.fp: Convenience and travel explain many cases.

indicators.name: Pooled or omnibus access through intermediaries
indicators.canon: Pooled or omnibus access through intermediaries
indicators.desc: Intermediaries trade or transact on behalf of undisclosed underlying clients.
indicators.ctx: Intermediaries trade or transact on behalf of undisclosed underlying clients.
indicators.fp: Omnibus structures are routine in securities.
